title: Knowledge Check 4 - Lessons 16-20
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 16-20 - Data 360 Setup and Administration | Data Source Connection and Ingestion. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A CRM data stream fed from an external Salesforce org started failing after a field was deleted. Where should the admin check what changed?
options: The home org's Setup Audit Trail only
The connected org's Setup Audit Trail for deleted custom field actions around the error date
The Feature Manager
The data space prefix
questions.explanation: Changes that break a stream fed by an external org are logged in the connected org's audit trail, so filter for deleted custom field actions near the error date. Checking only the home org's audit trail is the strongest distractor and is wrong because the object and field belong to the connected org.

questions.question: A manager asks which tool shows a complete unified view of one customer for validation. What is it?
options: Query Editor
Profile Explorer
Data Stream Control Center
Feature Manager
questions.explanation: Profile Explorer shows a complete unified profile for an individual or account, which is how you validate identity resolution output. The Data Stream Control Center is the strongest distractor and is wrong because it monitors stream status and quality, not unified profile contents.

questions.question: An admin needs a durable record of permission set and integration changes for compliance. What is the recommended action?
options: Rely on Salesforce's built-in retention indefinitely
Download the Setup Audit Trail periodically and store it externally
Enable tag propagation
Query the Problem Records DLO
questions.explanation: Salesforce retains a limited audit history, so the recommended practice is to download the Setup Audit Trail on a cadence and store it in an external log or SIEM system. Relying on built-in retention is the strongest distractor and is wrong because the history is not retained indefinitely.

questions.question: A team ingests clickstream events continuously and must trigger a real-time activation within seconds of an event. Which transformation capability fits?
options: A batch data transform scheduled every 15 minutes
A streaming data transform that reads the events and writes the prepared output
A data stream rerun with full refresh every hour
An identity resolution ruleset
questions.explanation: Streaming transforms process records as they arrive and are active immediately, delivering near-real-time preparation. The strongest distractor, a 15 minute batch transform, still adds up to 15 minutes of latency and cannot meet a requirement measured in seconds.

questions.question: Which task is the best fit for a batch data transform rather than a streaming data transform?
options: Joining three objects, aggregating, and preparing an object for identity resolution on a nightly cadence
Reacting to a single event the moment it is ingested
Writing output within seconds of an abandoned cart
Serving a real-time activation trigger
questions.explanation: A batch transform is a repeatable series of operations run manually or on a schedule and is built for heavy joins and aggregation. The strongest distractor, reacting the moment an event is ingested, describes exactly the latency profile that batch cannot provide.

questions.question: Which statement about streaming data transforms is TRUE?
options: They can be edited at any time after saving
They activate immediately when saved and cannot be modified, only deleted and recreated
Their source and target objects must be the same object
They can only write to data lake objects
questions.explanation: Help documents that streaming transforms activate on save and cannot be changed afterward. The distractor that says source and target must be the same object is the opposite of the rule, which requires them to be different objects.

questions.question: Which node would an architect add to stack rows from two different input objects into one flow?
options: Join
Append
Aggregate
Filter
questions.explanation: Append stacks rows from multiple inputs, which is exactly stacking. The strongest distractor, join, combines rows on matching keys and produces a wider result rather than a longer one.

questions.question: An architect needs to concatenate two fields and convert a text column to a date inside a batch transform. Where does that work happen?
options: In the data stream mapping
In a transform node, which groups transformations and formulas that run in sequence
In the identity resolution ruleset
In the target DMO definition
questions.explanation: A transform node groups transformations and formulas; built-in transformations include concatenation and column type conversion, and custom formulas can be added. The distractor of doing it in the data stream mapping is wrong because mapping relates fields, it does not concatenate or convert values.

questions.question: What is the role of the definition name on a batch data transform?
options: It replaces the transform name in the UI
It identifies a specific transform definition and lets you combine multiple definitions into a single transform
It sets the refresh schedule
It names the target data lake object
questions.explanation: Help states that each batch transform has a transform name and a definition name, and the definition name identifies specific transform definitions and lets you combine several into one transform. The distractor about the refresh schedule is wrong because scheduling is a separate run setting.

questions.question: A developer finishes a streaming data transform and must correct a column name in the SQL after saving. What must they do?
options: Edit the transform and save again
Delete the transform and create a new one, because streaming transforms cannot be modified after saving
Pause the transform, edit it, then resume
Change the column at the target DMO and it updates automatically
questions.explanation: Streaming transforms activate on save and cannot be changed, so the only path is delete and recreate. The strongest distractor, editing and saving again, is wrong because an active streaming transform is not editable.

questions.question: While creating a streaming data transform, which setting creates fully qualified keys on a newly created target object?
options: The Enable Value Suggestion field
The key qualifier, paired with a primary key field
The currency setting
The data space selection
questions.explanation: During target creation you choose a key qualifier to create fully qualified keys and then select a primary key field. The value suggestion distractor only offers valid values for fields, and the currency setting only normalizes multi-currency data.

questions.question: Which statement about a streaming data transform's source and target objects is TRUE?
options: They may be the same object
They must be different objects
The target object cannot be created during setup
The source must always be a data lake object
questions.explanation: Help states that the source and target objects must be different objects. The distractor that the target cannot be created during setup is wrong because you can select Create New, and the source can be a data model object or a data lake object.

questions.question: An external partner pushes order changes every few seconds and also uploads a full CSV each day. Which Data 360 connector handles both without a second data stream?
options: SFTP
The Ingestion API connector, whose streaming and bulk patterns can serve the same data stream
MuleSoft alone
A standard CRM data bundle
questions.explanation: The Ingestion API is a REST interface that offers a streaming pattern for incremental updates and a bulk pattern for periodic CSV loads, and the same data stream can accept both. The strongest distractor, SFTP, would handle the file but not the low-latency streaming updates.

questions.question: Which statement about mappings and relationships for a custom data stream is TRUE?
options: They are created automatically for every data stream
They are created automatically only for streams deployed through standard data bundles, so custom streams need them set up manually
They are not needed before segmentation
They are created by the connector when it is saved
questions.explanation: Help states that mappings and relationships are set up automatically only for data streams deployed through standard data bundles, and you must ensure they are correct for custom streams. The distractor that they are not needed before segmentation is wrong because only mapped fields and objects with relationships can be used for segmentation and activation.

questions.question: Which approach keeps a large external dataset in its source system while still letting Data 360 query it?
options: A full refresh data stream
Data federation or zero copy with caching or acceleration
A delete file on an incremental data stream
A streaming data transform
questions.explanation: Federation and zero copy let you use the data where it lives, and enabling caching or acceleration creates an accelerated data lake object for it. The full refresh distractor physically copies all rows, which is the opposite of leaving the data in place.
